title: Taifa of Tortosa
capsule: The Taifa of Tortosa was an independent Muslim principality at the mouth of the Ebro, founded around 1010 by the Slavic warlord Labib al-Fata al-Saqlabi following the collapse of the Caliphate of Córdoba, and ruled successively by the Saqlabi and then Huddid dynasties. The taifa controlled a strategically vital junction of river and coastal trade routes between Valencia and the Aragonese frontier, functioning as a multilingual commercial center in the northeast of al-Andalus. After a first period of independence ending with absorption by Zaragoza in 1060, a second autonomous phase under the Huddid dynasty lasted from 1081 until Almoravid conquest around 1099; the city was subsequently taken by Ramon Berenguer IV of Barcelona in 1148.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The taifa's core territory around Tortosa and the lower Ebro is reasonably documented in Arabic chronicles; inland extents are not systematically recorded and must be estimated from the known geography of neighboring polities.
